key_insight: Entrance effects in lab-scale DCMD are Reynolds-number dependent: near-inlet vortices reshape temperature polarization, and the bias can flip from stronger to weaker TP as flow rate increases.
engineering_relevance: Membrane distillation correlations and module comparisons should account for geometry- and Reynolds-specific entrance bias, rather than applying a single constant correction.
method: 3D CFD of direct contact membrane distillation modules
Swept inlet Reynolds number from 10 to 1000
Compared side-chamber length and main-channel height effects on flow, kinetic energy, and TP
evidence_signal: The study used numerical simulations across multiple geometries and Reynolds numbers, showing vortex persistence and TP deviations that change with operating condition.
watch_item: Entrance corrections from lab-scale modules may not transfer universally, because the bias depends on geometry and Reynolds number and can change direction.
paper_title: Reynolds-number-dependent entrance bias in temperature polarization of lab-scale membrane distillation
